Luca: Heads up — onboarding Cormorant-7B-hybrid hit a weird longctx regression on our smoke suite.
Anya: ah ok what kind of regression? :eyes:
Luca: Short repro: generation drifts after ~1k tokens, logits look fine but replies become incoherent. KV-cache mismatch suspected.
Sam: Any tokenizer diffs? those usually bite us.
Luca: Yes. Tokenizer dump shows ZWJ (U+200D) sequences breaking into unexpected token ids vs our qwen/gemma baselines.
Luca: Example:
```
input = "Dr. A\u200DSmith went to..."
tokens_corm = [101, 2345, 9001, 77, 12]
tokens_ref  = [101, 2345, 9001, 78, 12]  # off by one at the ZWJ boundary
```
Rachel: That would explain prefix cache lookup misses and shifting KV indices.
Anya: Could be a vocab normalization difference (NFKC vs NFC) or a tokenizer merge rule. Did we try the normalizer settings?
Luca: Ran quick check — model's tokenizer uses an internal patch: keeps ZWJ as separate token instead of merging with preceding grapheme. Changing normalization to NFKC in the conversion script makes token ids line up.
Sam: Interesting. But the longctx drift also looks like headwise rotary mismatches in attention when we run int3 quant.
Luca: Right. With fp16 load the outputs match after normalizer fix. With int3 quant the per-head rotary scale seems to distort phase for odd heads.
Luca: Debug log (simplified):
```
HEAD 0 rotary_scale = 1.0002
HEAD 1 rotary_scale = 0.9978
HEAD 2 rotary_scale = 1.0001
... (post-int3 calibration)
```
Luca: The original trained model had per-head rotary scaling baked in; our int3 packer uses a shared scale table that likely gets clustered incorrectly.
Rachel: Could be centroiding in kmeans quantizer merging head scales. Did you try per-head calibration runs (no clustering) vs global clustering?
Luca: Yes — per-head calibration keeps coherence, but increases model size and latency. Global clustering yields the drift.
Anya: For onboarding checklist: tokenizer normalization fix + ensure quantizer keeps per-head scale (or falls back to fp16 for heads with >eps variance). Also add a smoke that runs longctx generation for 2k tokens.
Sam: Agreed. Also add a small heuristic: if tokenization mismatches against our canonical tokenizer for >0.5% tokens on sample set, fail the conversion and surface diff.
triage-bot: New triage item created: #TRIAGE-1147 — "Cormorant longctx drift: ZWJ tokenizer + int3 rotary-scale clustering" (assignee: Anya)
Anya: I'll pick this up. Plan: (1) patch conversion to NFKC, (2) add token-diff gate, (3) re-run int3 with per-head scale option and collect eval metrics.
Rachel: For evals, include perplexity on BookWiki long spans and our hallucination prompt-set. Capture token alignment diffs as histogram.
Luca: Running an expedited int3 job now with per-head scale, will post results in this thread.
Sam: If per-head costs too much, we can try a hybrid: cluster heads with similar variance and keep outliers per-head.
Luca: Good idea. Also discovered one other quirk: model's embedding projection order is [proj_out, proj_in] vs our runtime expecting [proj_in, proj_out]. That explains cross-model scoring differences.
Luca: Converison patch candidate:
```
# swap linear weight order for embedding proj
W = orig_weights.reshape(2, D, D)
proj_in = W[1]
proj_out = W[0]
```
Anya: Oof. That would definitely scramble KV indexing if left unnoticed. Add explicit shape+checksum assertions in conversion pipeline.
triage-bot: Update: TRIAGE-1147 status -> in_progress (by Anya)
Luca: quick update: per-head int3 run completed, early numbers:
- BookWiki long-ppl: fp16=12.3, int3-perhead=12.6, int3-global=15.8
- Hallucination rate: fp16 baseline 4.1%, int3-perhead 4.3%, int3-global 9.8%
Luca: So per-head is OK, global clustering is catastrophic for quality.
Rachel: Those numbers are convincing — we should prefer per-head quant by default for Cormorant family models.
Sam: Also enforce tokenizer normalization gate. I'll add CI lint that runs token-diff on a small corpus.
Anya: I'll push conversion + tests today, then we can promote to dedicated onboarding lane.
Luca: Thanks team. Will follow up with the exact conversion PR and the quant config diff. :shipit:
Rachel: nice work — saved us from a nasty production surprise.
summary: Onboard cormorant-7b-hybrid encountered long-context drift caused by tokenizer ZWJ handling and int3 quant rotary-scale clustering. Short-term fix: convert tokenizer normalization to NFKC and use per-head quant calibration. Added TRIAGE-1147 and action items: token-diff gate, per-head quant fallback, checksum assertions for embedding proj order.
